disease_label_per_paper: COVID-19 with hemoptysis and hematuria as initial symptoms
presentation_summary: 21-year-old Afghan man presented with seven days of fever, chills, hemoptysis, and hematuria.
Admission exam showed tachypnea, tachycardia, normal blood pressure, oxygen saturation 86% on room air improving to 96% with 60% Venturi oxygen, and bilateral coarse crackles.
Labs showed WBC 11.61 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 14.7 g/dL, platelets 162 x10^9/L, D-dimer 900 ng/mL, CRP 12 mg/dL, and ESR 60 mm/h.
Urinalysis showed protein 1+, WBC 12-14, RBC 20-25, and blood 2+.
Chest CT showed bilateral ground-glass opacities and multifocal consolidation along subpleural regions; SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR was positive.
Blood and urine cultures showed no growth; sputum studies were negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and bacterial infection.
